TESTIMONY OF
Deirdre Gilbert
Department of Marine Resources
The Department of Marine Resources (DMR) is testifying
ln Support of
LD 489 An Act to Provide for a Vessel Breakdown License Exception for Commercial Halibut Fishing License Holders Before the Committee on Marine Resources Sponsored by Representative Strout Date of Hearing: March 6, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members ofthe Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Deirdre Gilbert, I am the Director of State Marine Policy for the Department of Marine Resources and I am testifying on behalf of the Department in support of LD 489.
LD 489 is similar to other bills that this committee has previously addressed on the topic of vessel breakdowns, for such commercial fisheries as scallops, urchins, and menhaden. First, it provides a helpful clarification consistent with other licenses that the license holder's authority to conduct the licensed activities is limited to the vessel listed on the license. In addition, it provides the commissioner with the authority to grant an exception to this limitation, such that a license holder could be authorized to use a vessel other than the vessel listed on their license in the event that the
vessel has become temporarily inoperable, because of an accident or mechanical breakdown.
For clarity, at any point, a license holder could contact the Department to have the vessel identified on
their license changed to a different vessel. However, for many fisheries, the problem is that the license holder wants to list a vessel that another license holder has already listed, and there is some limitation on the fishery that is applied as a vessel limit. In the case of halibut, no more than 25 tags may be assigned to a specific vessel. Therefore, if your boat breaks down and you want to identify a
different vessel that another halibut license holder has already identified, it is likely that there are already 25 tags assigned to that vessel. This exception would allow the commissioner to authorize
more than one license holder to list the same vessel when the requirements for the exception are met and therefore, for a limited time, more than 25 tags could be assigned to a single vessel.
At this time, the state halibut season lasts from May 18 to lune 13. The proposed legislation would allow for one 2 week waiver, which could be extended by an additional 2 weeks. Therefore, this
waiver could be used to cover the entirety of a halibut season. While the Department has no
objection to providing the necessary flexibility to allow a license holder to continue to operate, we also
want to ensure that these waivers do not become workarounds that are used on an annual basis as a long-term strategy for two license holders to fish from the same vessel. For this reason, we would recommend a further limitation that a breakdown waiver may not be issued in consecutive seasons.
Thank you for your consideration, and l would be happy to answer any questions you might have.

To: Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Marine Resources From: Emily Coffin, Policy Coordinator Date: March 6th, 2025
Re: LD 489: An Act to Provide For a Vessel Breakdown License Exception for Commercial Halibut Fishing License Holders (Emergency)
Dear Honorable Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and distinguished members of the Joint Committee on Marine Resources:
The Maine Coast Fishermen's Association (MCFA) is an industry-based nonprofit dedicated to restoring the fisheries of the Gulf of Maine and preserving Maine's iconic fishing communities for future generations. Founded by Maine fishermen to provide a voice in fisheries management, MCFA represents many halibut fishermen who rely on the species to bolster their business and diversify their fishing practice.
MCFA is in support of LD 489 and its effort to provide fishermen the flexibility to continue fishing if their primary vessel is temporarily out of commission. The halibut season is very short (less than a month) and if a fisherman who relies on halibut suffers an unlucky mechanical issue or worse, they would suffer a loss of vital income. A 2-week exception to the standard regulation tying fishermen to their vessel would allow for much needed flexibility in the time of mishap. Those who work and live around boats know all too well that engine troubles and other misfortunes happen to everyone. For the Marine Resource Committee to allow the opportunity for a fisherman to request a reprieve from the rule to participate in a short fishing window would surely benefit Maine's fishermen and the economy writ large.
Thank you, Emily Coffin, Policy Coordinator Maine Coast Fishermen's Association

Public Testimony In Support of LD 489 -- An Act to Provide for a Vessel Breakdown License Exception for Commercial Halibut Fishing License Holders

Presented by Representative Strout of Harrington -- District 11
Good morning, Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler and distinguished members of the Marine Resources Committee. l am
Representative Tiffany Strout from Harrington, representing the towns of Milbridge, Harrington, Columbia, Columbia Falls, Centerville,
Addison, Jonesport, Beals, Jonesboro, Roque Bluffs, Whitneyville and Machias and I am here today to provide testimony in support of LD 489 An Act to Provide for a Vessel Breakdown License Exception for Commercial Halibut Fishing License Holders.

I was approached by a constituent to see if l would put in a bill to address a situation last year that resulted in her missing the 2024
halibut season.

The season for halibut fishing is very short going from sunrise on May 18"` to sunset on June 13"` . In addition to the short season, as with other fishing industries, there are regulations to help with sustainability of the industry. Some of these regulations include, a minimum size of 41 inches to keep the fish, the fishery is open access meaning there are no restrictions to obtain a license, you also have to purchase tags, there is a limit of 25 halibut tags per fisherman, the tags must be assigned to a fishing vessel and Atlantic
halibut cannot be transferred between vessels.

Last year my constitute was in the process of getting a new motor put in her boat. This project extended into the halibut fishing season resulting in her not being able to fish. Her husband is a commercial fisherman, who also fishes for halibut and there are other family
members who fish for halibut, but with the current law she was not able to transfer her tags onto another vessel. The law states only 25

tags can be assigned to any one vessel.

.

This bill focuses on modifying a few parts of the tagging requirements specifically, all tags must be declared to one vessel, a vessel
may have only one license holder's tags assigned to that vessel, vessels may land a maximum of 25 Atlantic halibut per year, it is illegal for more than one type (recreational or commercial) of landing tag to be assigned to any one vessel per year, and no individual may
`
possess more than one type of landing tag per year.

If this bill were to pass, it would provide an opportunity for individuals who may end up overrunning on maintenance for their vessel or if
they have a vessel issue that occurs during the halibut season to reach out to the Commissioner of the Department of Marine Resources and ask for a breakdown exception on their vessel. Should the Commissioner grant the waiver, this would allow the
fisherman to then assign their tags to another boat, even if that boat has 25 halibut tags already assigned to it.

Other fisheries have something like this in place and this would follow the same approval process as those industries.

Thank you for your time today and I would be glad to answer any questions.

Sincerely,
